messages:
alex_k: Kestrel is reporting repeated 429s and high 95th latency during a campaign spike this morning. They say baseline QPS ~120, peak ~950 for ~8 minutes and the dedicated pool is 4 GPUs. seeing throttles and timeouts.
priya_r: :eyes: Do we have their pool config and autoscale policy? 4 GPUs sounds undersized for ~1k peak.
john_m: I grabbed the pool config and initial metrics: autoscale min=4, max=6, target_util=0.7, scale_cooldown=300s. Their avg token/sec per GPU ~150 during baseline, but during spike GPU util jumped to 94% and request queue grew.
sasha_ops: Can you paste the policy and a short metric dump?
mike_support: Pasting snippet from Kestrel's Dedicated settings:```
resource_pool: kestrel-prod
gpus: 4
autoscale:
  min: 4
  max: 6
  target_utilization: 0.7
  scale_up_threshold: 0.8
  scale_down_threshold: 0.5
  cooldown_seconds: 300
concurrency_per_gpu: 24
request_timeout_ms: 12000
```
alex_k: Metric samples (1m rollup at spike start): ```
2026-03-15T08:12:00Z gpu_util: [0.88,0.92,0.95,0.94]
request_rate: 940 qps
active_workers: 96
queue_depth: 320
429_count: 412
average_lat_95: 820ms
```
priya_r: So they hit queue_depth 320 and we returned 429s. With concurrency_per_gpu 24 * 4 = 96 workers, queue exceeded capacity. Autoscaler didn't add nodes fast enough (cooldown 300s) and max=6 might not be enough for a sudden 8-minute burst.
john_m: Two things to check: noisy neighbor (sibling tenants on same hosts), and whether KV cache cold-start increased per-request work. Sasha, can you run a noisy-tenant check on kestrel-prod host set?
sasha_ops: Running quick check now. ops-bot: noisy-neighbor-scan started for pool kestrel-prod. ETA ~90s.
ops-bot: noisy-neighbor-scan complete. results: 1 host at 97% shared_mem, 2 hosts with background batch jobs (high memcpy). risk_score: medium.
mike_support: Also saw elevated token generation per request during the spike (avg tokens/request went from 28 -> 62) — likely marketing prompt variation. That explains higher CPU/GPU work per request.
alex_k: Customer says they didn't change prompts. Could be A/B test on their side. For immediate mitigation: recommend temporarily raising max to 10, reduce cooldown to 60s, and increase concurrency_per_gpu to 32 if safe. Also enable burst capacity (if available) to avoid 429s while new nodes spin up.
priya_r: Agreed. Proposed runbook steps for on-call: 1) escalate to SRE for noisy neighbor eviction, 2) push config change to increase max GPUs to 10 and cooldown to 60s, 3) enable burst mode for kestrel-prod, 4) monitor 95/99 lat and 429s for next 30m, 5) follow up with Kestrel about possible prompt/traffic change.
john_m: Repro steps for us to validate locally before config change: 1) replay Kestrel traffic capture (s3://redwood-captures/kestrel/2026-03-15-spike) with token distribution adjusted to 62 tokens/request, 2) run against a 4-gpu pool, then 6-gpu, then 10-gpu and measure queue depth & 429s.
sasha_ops: I kicked off a replay against a staging pool (4 GPUs) — initial results look like queue blowup at ~700 qps when avg tokens ~60. With 10 GPUs queue stays <50 and no 429s.
mike_support: Customer-facing note: "We're investigating throttling during your spike. Preliminary findings: pool hit utilization limits and autoscaler cooldown prevented fast scale-up. We're applying temporary capacity and configs now to stabilize. We'll follow up with root cause and recommended reserved sizing"
alex_k: I'll apply the emergency config now (increase max->10, cooldown->60s, enable burst). tagging @priya_r for approval.
priya_r: Approved. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: config-change applied to kestrel-prod: max_gpus=10, cooldown_seconds=60, burst_mode=enabled by alex_k. change_id: cfg-20260315-4821
john_m: After change (5m later) metrics: ```
2026-03-15T08:20:00Z request_rate: 930 qps
gpu_util (post-scale): [0.62,0.59,0.61,0.58,0.51,0.50,0.49,0.48,0.46,0.45]
queue_depth: 22
429_count_last_5m: 12
lat_95: 210ms
```
sasha_ops: Noisy neighbor remediation: we evicted a background batch job from host-12 which dropped shared_mem usage to 32% and memcpy to normal. ops-bot: eviction completed.
mike_support: Customer confirmed decreased 429s and latency within 30 minutes. They're asking for recommended steady-state sizing guidance for recurring campaigns.
\alex_k: Recommendation: for baseline 120 qps with campaign peaks ~1k qps lasting <15m, reserve 8 GPUs or set autoscale max 12 with target_util 0.65 and cooldown 90s. Also suggest prefix caching for common prompts and token budgeting.
priya_r: Also propose an alert rule: if queue_depth > 100 for >2m or 429_rate > 1% trigger paging and auto-scaling emergency to +50% capacity.
\ohn_m: small typo in my earlier msg -> should be john_m. :grimacing:
\alex_k: Good catch. Final action items: - SRE to document noisy neighbor findings and hosts evicted (sasha_ops) - Update customer sizing doc and quota (mike_support) - Add replay test to CI to catch similar token spikes (john_m) - Follow up with customer about prompt changes (alex_k).
priya_r: Thanks team. I'll schedule a postmortem with Kestrel for next week. :calendar:
